obligations.note: At head, required_approvals returns 2 only when amount > policy.DUAL_CONTROL_THRESHOLD. PAY-1 requires two distinct approvers for a payment at or above the approved threshold of 10000.00, so an amount equal to the threshold now needs only one approval.
Ticket CHG-25446 is approved by change manager Erik Brandt before review, and its components payments.payments and payments.tests cover payments.py and tests/test_approvals_remaining.py.
Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver and not the author Jonah Weiss, approved a code_review of the head commit.
The code_review approval names head commit 6cad16a4d04a700219498dfeda8c562cb296f656, so it covers the merged tree with no later commits.
CI succeeded on a62c4dd, not on the final commit. The later commit changes the dual-control comparison from >= to >, which is a behavior change, so the earlier run does not count.
The touched components payments.payments and payments.tests are not marked security_sensitive, so a security_review approval is not required.
The change does not touch protected controls data, control tests, or CI paths, so a control_owner approval is not required.
Ticket CHG-25446 is type standard and the change record is not an emergency, so no post-implementation review is due.

The strict greater-than comparison is a deviation from PAY-1, and the register has no approved, unexpired exception scoped to PAY-1 and payments.payments. The listed exceptions are for other obligations, expired, or withdrawn.

Ledger entry ACR-0401's exhaustive proof covers required_approvals at an older commit, and this change alters that comparison. That proof does not cover the head, and the dual-control control test ran only on the earlier commit, so there is no replacement exhaustive evidence on the final code.

summary: The payments-queue change also flips dual control from at-or-above to strictly above the approved 10000.00 threshold, so a payment equal to the threshold can be released with one approver. That violates PAY-1, and no in-force exception covers it. The prior exhaustive proof of required_approvals no longer applies, and the green CI run is on the earlier commit, before that behavior change, so testing and evidence continuity fail as well.
